parts:
Dear unmarked users,
 This is slightly off topic but since I'm effectively in charge around here I've decided to bend the rules for my own benefit. Sorry about that.
 
 If someone can tell me what's wrong with this code below, I will buy you a beer at the next TWS meeting and we can discuss fun things related to unmarked.
 
 This code below simulates a capture-recapture data set for a population subject to sample K = 8 times (N=100 individuals).  Then I have a likelihood function for "model Mh" where logit(p[i]) ~ normal(mu, sigma^2).
 The likelihood is based on the standard binomial likelihood for individual encounters but integrated over the random effects distribution.  In this case I'm evaluting the integral by just adding up the area of a few hundred rectangles. (note: I was originally using the integrate() function but that doesn't work either).
 
 I have it set now to mimic model M0 (by fixing sigma = small number) which I did as a debugging test.  
 This is clearly not working (run it a few times and you will see).  If you change back to simulating data with heterogeneity in p and with sigma as a free parameter of the likelihood it still doesn't work.
 
 The model seems to work if I change from the Bernoulli encounters to binomial frequencies.  (remove the "prod" from the likelihood and change the ym to sum(ym) and change 1 to K in the binomial argument).
 
 I can't imagine where the issue could be here. I suspect some obvious glaring thing that is so minor that my eyes look right over it.... (for 2 days now).
 
thanks all!
andy
 
 
 

N<- 100
K<- 8
# Simulate a data set. In this case with constant p but can change to heterogeneity
y<- matrix(0,nrow=N,ncol=K)
for(i in 1:N){
  p<- plogis(-1.8)  #rnorm(1,-1.85, 0.5))
  y[i,]<- rbinom(K, 1, p)
  }

# observed data set, nind x K
y<- y[apply(y,1,sum)>0,]

# Need this
expit<- function(x){  1/(1+exp(-x)) }
 
# Likelihood function with sigma fixed (near 0) result should be close to Model M0 result
Mhlik <-function(parms, y2d, sigma=0.1){

# Just two parameters
mu<- parms[1]
#sigma<-exp(parms[2])
n0<-exp(parms[2])
K<- ncol(y2d)
nind<- nrow(y2d)

# add a row of zeros onto the matrix
y2d<- rbind(y2d, rep(0,K))
# a vector to hold the result
il<-rep(NA,nrow(y2d))

# loop over rows of y2d and compute the marginal likelihood by evaluating the integral on a fine grid
# (note: the "integrate" function doesn't work either..... )
for(i in 1:nrow(y2d) ){
 ym <- as.vector(y2d[i,])
 eta.gr<- seq(-8,8,.05)
 f<-  function(eta,sig=sigma){
      prod(dbinom(ym,1, expit(mu+eta), log=FALSE))*dnorm(eta,0,sig)
  }
 f.gr<- f(eta.gr)
 # Marginal likelihood right here:
 il[i]<- sum(f.gr*0.025)

}
# Sum this stuff up
-1*(    lgamma(n0+nind+1) - lgamma(n0+1) + sum(c(rep(1,nind),n0)*log(il)))
}


nlm(Mhlik,c(-1,1), y2d=y)

    f <-  function(eta, sig = sigma){

    }

Here are 10 or so iterations which show that the estimates of Nhat for both likelihoods are now about right (truth : N = 100).
 Thanks Bill and Murray, a pint of Guiness on me!
regards
andy
